content:
anya: Quick RFC follow-up. We still need to pick a practical approach for high-cardinality attrs: full tenant partitioning, strict gateway eviction, or a middle path.

mike: My quick take: strict eviction is cheapest but breaks billing fidelity occasionally. Full partitioning is expensive ops-wise.

tariq: We had a billing incident when billing.customer_id was trimmed. Customer impact was real. So fidelity matters for a subset of tenants.

lucy: Noisy tenants also spike query latency. If we can contain them, overall platform UX improves.

anya: Proposed middle path: pinned attrs + slimming + short-term fanout for noisy tenants. Keep ops bounded.

mike: Fanout semantics: write slimmed event to main stream and full event to tenant stream when promoted. Query layer uses tenant stream when present.

tariq: Detector idea: 5m sliding window using unique-attr growth rate + TPS. Promote if both exceed thresholds; add cooldown to avoid flapping.

lucy: Add a safelist for enterprise customers that always get full fidelity. Also soft-flag missing pinned attrs instead of dropping traces.

anya: Gateway config sketch: pinned_attrs=["billing.customer_id","tenant.id","service.name"], max_extra=25, missing_policy="flag"; fanout: tps=800, unique_growth=400/min, window=2h, cooldown=30m, max_dedicated=30.

mike: Ops note: cap concurrent dedicated streams and require manual approval for >30. That keeps cost bounded.

tariq: Spike plan: synth load (200 tenants, 5 noisy), measure write amplification, cost delta, and attribution_loss. I'll prototype detector + cooldown.

ingest-bot: spike created by @anya -> PHAB-OBS-999 (https://phab.redwood/OBS-999).

anya: Action owners: tariq + mike run 4d spike, lucy prepares attribution evals, i'll update RFC with numbers and a playbook. Post results here.

lucy: I'll include prompt-based evals to surface false negatives on billing attribution.

mike: ack, will post progress in-thread. :thumbsup:
